newsitem.title: UK: Blair says Britain unlikely to join EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Blair says Britain unlikely to join EMU in 1999.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday that it was highly unlikely that Britain would want to join a single European currency in the first wave, which is scheduled for 1999.
Answering questions in parliament, he also said it would be better for economic and monetary union (EMU) not to go ahead at all than for it to start with "fudged" convergence criteria.
"It is highly unlikely that Britain would want to join the first wave of monetary union," Blair said.
"We have always said that the criteria for monetary union should not be fiddled or fudged or botched in any way and if they are, then the answer is not to delay, the answer is not to proceed."

Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said earlier that the government's position on a single European currency was unchanged. It would maintain its "wait-and-see" stance while acknowledging there are big obstacles to joining in the first round.
"Our position on the single currency has not changed," Brown told reporters.
